annotations.text:
RepoPulse — shipped UI, drawn from the real components.
Tokens are lifted verbatim from apps/web/src/styles/theme.css (dark theme). Every element on these boards corresponds to a component in apps/web/src/widgets/**; nothing here is proposed or invented. Where the shipped screen differs from UX_SPEC §4, the note beside the board says so.

Org Overview carries MORE than UX_SPEC §4.a sketches: Weekly pulse (pinned top), Improvement plan (D9), Security rollup, Top risks and Risk axes were all added after the spec was written. The health tiles ship WITHOUT the sparkline the spec drew — name, badge and basis only.

Repo Detail ships SEVEN routed tabs, not the five in §4.b — Security (W8) and Code Health (W9) were added later. Each tab is its own URL, so it is linkable and back-button-able. The 'why?' popover is shown open: the score is never displayed without its basis label and formula breakdown.

The Code Health tab IS fully implemented — its components live in routes/repos/$repoId/code-health.tsx, which is why widgets/code-health/ holds only contracts.ts. Same discipline as Security: an unrun scanner reads 'not measured', never 0, because a zero is a claim about the repository that an unrun scanner has not earned.

PR Detail is the board that diverges MOST from its spec. §4.c drew a horizontal stage bar, risk badges, a findings accordion with evidence quotes, per-file hotspot badges and a GitHub ↗ link. What ships is a vertical stage list, a size chip, review/checks side by side, a plain files table — and an 'Automated review' panel that is permanently empty because Tier-2 (W6) has not run. Per FR-WEB-8 it says WHY it is empty rather than looking like a clean bill of health.

File drill-down. Two things the spec did not have: the Intent control (Refactor / Supervise / Acknowledged, W6-09) sits FIRST because what a team means to do about a file is context for every number under it, and the history banner reports 'last seen' and previous paths WITHOUT claiming the file was deleted — ingestion cannot tell a deletion from a quiet file.

Churn bars are grouped, not stacked: rework is a subset of gross, and stacking would read as double the churn that actually happened.

CORRECTION TO THE SPEC. UX_SPEC §4.e calls the Findings Explorer "v1.x, shell ships in MVP as a teaser" — that is stale. The full explorer SHIPPED in W6-04: six URL-synced filters (the scanner facet driven by the registry, so a later wave's scanner becomes filterable with no edit here), bulk confirm/dismiss behind a REQUIRED note, and a false-positive-rate widget. What is still a teaser is the repo-level Findings TAB, not this screen.

The FP rate shows an em dash, never 0%, when nothing has been triaged: an untriaged corpus must not read as a flawless model (FR-INSIGHTS-1).

My Focus. N-9 forbids cross-person comparison, so there is no leaderboard and no 'you vs the team' framing anywhere — every number is the caller's own. §4.f's personal-cycle-time-vs-repo-median chart is NOT shipped; four count tiles stand in its place, and they are captioned 'not compared to an earlier window' rather than showing a delta they never computed.

Two states the screen keeps apart: identity-unlinked (fixable — re-authorize) and nothing-to-do. Both render empty lists, and telling someone they have no work when we simply cannot find them is the worse failure. The since-last-visit strip appears only when something actually changed.

Custom Views. The starter-template gallery stays on screen even once views exist — the SECOND view is harder to design than the first, and the templates are the only place the widget vocabulary is visible outside edit mode. Templates are filtered by the viewer's persona (§6).

Not drawn, because it is a separate route rather than part of this screen: the drag-resize edit mode on /views/:id. 'home' and 'shared' are marked with a glyph AND a word — never colour alone (§7).

Report Center. FIVE report types ship, not the four §4.h lists — Code Health (D11) was added in W9. Two things the spec never had: a free-text 'Context' annotation stored WITH the report, and a compare mode that diffs two runs when exactly two rows are ticked.

Status is a glyph plus a word (◷ queued / ◐ running / ✓ ready / ✕ failed), never colour alone. The list polls every 3s rather than opening an SSE channel: a report takes seconds, and a dedicated event stream would be more moving parts than the problem deserves. PDF is a plain link, not fetch() — the download streams behind the session check and never lands in JS memory.

Plans (D9). The detail that defines this screen: there is NO 'mark done' button anywhere. An item closes when its metric actually moves, verified nightly (W5-06) — a human cannot declare victory over a number. Every item shows its verify criterion in plain language BEFORE anyone commits to it, and cites evidence keys rather than copying the data, so a reader can go and check.

Regressed items are styled warn and pinned. The T2 summary uses the quiet-accent AI card family (R-D3): a provenance chip reading 'T2 · local — reworded, numbers computed', no gradient, no sparkle. On a Tier-1-only install plans work fully and this card is simply absent.

Admin ships EIGHT tabs, not §4.i's four. Connections, Sync, Members and Analysis were specified; Identities, Agreements, Rules and Settings arrived with later waves.

Two things worth seeing drawn. The credential column shows a fingerprint and the last 4 only — the API returns exactly that for this display, because showing more would put a token in the DOM (SC-2). And the per-repo table surfaces the rate-limit budget as a column: budget is law (Law 7), so an operator has to see a repo approaching its limit BEFORE it goes paused_budget, not after.
